key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can non-destructively distinguish whether recombination losses in perovskite solar cells originate near the ETL/perovskite interface or deeper in the absorber, and it reveals that PEABF4 passivation slows initial interfacial loss but accelerates broader thermal degradation over time.
engineering_relevance: This offers a depth-sensitive diagnostic for evaluating interface treatments and aging mechanisms in perovskite solar cells, helping engineers target stability improvements without destructive sectioning.
method: Used wavelength-dependent PL excitation to probe different carrier generation depths.
Compared untreated and PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpreted PL decay trends with diffusion-recombination simulations to separate surface recombination velocity from bulk lifetime changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination from fullerene deposition initially, but under thermal stress the PL decay signatures broaden from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with worsening bulk and interfacial losses.
watch_item: PL-based depth interpretation is model-dependent, so excitation-depth assumptions and simulation parameters must be carefully validated for each stack architecture.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
